2. Unlabeled data: In this case, the language model is trained on unlabeled data, where the model is given a text as input but there is no corresponding label attached to the word. The model learns to predict the most likely word or words given the input text.

In either case, the model is trained to generate output that is grammatically correct and makes sense in context, based on the language and grammatical rules of the target language. For example, a language model trained on labeled data will learn to correctly categorize nouns, verbs, and adjectives, while a language model trained on unlabeled data will learn to produce sentences that are grammatically correct and make sense within the context of the input text.</s>
